title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection thresholds and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: The current perf canary detects regressions using fixed thresholds which cause both false-positives during noisy traffic windows and missed regressions for throughput-sensitive workloads. This PR introduces adaptive auto-detection of latency and throughput regressions and a rollout-guard layer that ties canary failure signals to rollout policies. Summary of changes: 1) Add adaptive thresholding in perf-canary service: dynamic baselining using sliding-window percentile aggregates and robust statistics (median absolute deviation) to tolerate noise. 2) Introduce a configurable RolloutGuard component that ingests canary signals and enforces rollout actions (pause, rollback, alert) based on policy rules (severity, blackout windows, confidence). 3) Improve observability: new canary scoring metric, per-route regression telemetry, and alert annotations. 4) CI/perf harness: synthetic workload scenarios added to exercise throughput regressions and noisy latency spikes. 5) Docs and runbook updates describing failure modes and recovery steps. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear ticket linked ENG-2128 - [x] Unit and integration tests for detector and guard - [x] End-to-end perf test scenarios in CI - [x] Docs and runbook changes - [x] Canary rollout policy templates for ops Backwards compatibility: fully additive; rollout guard is opt-in per-deployment and uses existing canary API. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag; staged rollout to perf-canary stack then to production canary traffic for 48h in canary-mode before enabling auto-enforcement. Related work: builds on prior perf-canary auto-detect PRs (see pr-41286, pr-51731).
commits: feat(canary): adaptive threshold detector with MAD baseline
chore(ci): add synthetic throughput/latency scenarios to perf CI
feat(rollout): rollout guard component + policy evaluator
test(perf): add integration tests for noisy windows and throughput drop
docs: perf-canary runbook and policy examples
review_comments: Alicia Chen: Can you add a short note explaining why MAD was chosen over stddev for baseline? Author: MAD is more robust to outliers which is important for bursty traffic seen in internal workloads; added comment in detector.py.
Diego Ramos: Suggest exposing a max-change cap to avoid spurious rollbacks during cluster upgrades. Author: Added 'max_change_pct' to rollout policy and included tests for upgrade spike scenario.
Matt Johnson: CI perf job flaky on initial run (timing). Author: Increased synthetic workload duration and added retry on harness startup; CI reran and passed.
SRE (Sofia Alvarez): How does this interact with existing alerting? Author: We add annotations to alerts with canary_score and confidence; SRE can opt into auto-enforce via policy flags.
Security (Ethan Park): Any user-facing config that could be abused? Author: Policies are stored in cluster configmaps with RBAC gating; documented in security section of docs.
release_notes: Add adaptive perf canary detection with MAD-based baselining and a configurable RolloutGuard to automatically pause or rollback rollouts on detected latency/throughput regressions. Opt-in feature flag; docs include runbook and example policies.
regression_thresholds: default: latency: 95th > baseline + 3*MAD; throughput: drop > 10% with confidence > 90% (configurable)
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind CANARY_AUTO_GUARD flag. To enable: apply example_policy.yaml to namespace and monitor canary_score metric. Runbook updated in docs/perf-canary.md. If false positives observed, increase baseline window or widen max_change_pct.
human_summary: Implements adaptive detection and rollout guards to reduce false positives and automate safe rollout decisions for canary deployments. Added tests, CI scenarios and docs; merged to main behind a feature flag.
